title: Alfred Hitchcock's birth chart
metaDescription: Alfred Hitchcock's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 20.5° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 20.5° Leo, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Leo, but precisely: 20.5°, third decan, 20°–30°, under Mars in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 0.9° Virgo, Venus was at 11.3° Leo, Mars was at 4.7° Libra. Read together: a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Saturn and Pluto: 0.6° from an exact opposition. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner. Behind it, Mars sextile Uranus at 0.7°, and Mercury sextile Jupiter at 2.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has four entries for this chart. The Sun in Leo at 20.5° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; the Moon in Scorpio at 8.6° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mercury in Virgo at 0.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Libra at 4.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 fire, 3 air, 2 water, 1 earth by element and 5 mutable, 4 fixed, 1 cardinal by modality. Fire weights a chart toward initiative — starting, asserting, spending energy to find out what happens. Mercury and Saturn were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Scorpio for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.7° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 8.6°.
